The earlier attempt embedded a Markdown wrapper *as if it were* the `.fd` source — that's why the validator choked on `![...]` and `<sub>`. Here is the actual `X.fd` content:

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 block
title "Certificate renewal automation"

block scheduler "Scheduler"
block renewaljob "Renewal job"
block caclient "CA client"
block ca "Certificate authority"
block deployagent "Deploy agent"
block service "Service"

scheduler -> renewaljob
renewaljob -> caclient
caclient -> ca
renewaljob -> deployagent
deployagent -> service
```

Save that as `figures/cert-renewal.fd`, run it through `build-svg.js` to produce `figures/cert-renewal.svg`, and embed the two side by side in the host Markdown like this:

```markdown
![Certificate renewal automation: scheduler triggers a renewal job, which asks a CA client to obtain a certificate from the CA, then hands off to a deploy agent that restarts the service](figures/cert-renewal.svg)

<sub>source: [figures/cert-renewal.fd](figures/cert-renewal.fd)</sub>
```

The `.fd` file (fenced above) is what goes through the validator; the Markdown snippet is only the embed that references the built SVG — the two must not be conflated, which is exactly what tripped the first attempt.
